bottleneck.description: 100+ satellite RO/AIS/RF data constellation competing with PlanetiQ, GeoOptics, Kleos, HawkEye 360, and Unseenlabs in weather and RF-geolocation data services.

dependency.key_customers: NOAA, NASA, ESA, US Space Force, EUMETSAT, defense and intelligence agencies, Luxembourg Space Agency
dependency.key_suppliers: Glasgow in-house satellite manufacturing, SpaceX/Rocket Lab (launch), commercial GNSS receivers

editorial.notes: Spire operates ~100 LEMUR cubesats providing GNSS radio-occultation weather data, AIS/ADS-B tracking, and RF intelligence. Competitors include PlanetiQ and GeoOptics (RO weather), HawkEye 360 and Unseenlabs (RF geolocation), Kleos Space (RF), and ORBCOMM (AIS). Government customers (NOAA, ESA, NASA, DoD) explicitly multi-source data buys to avoid single-vendor lock-in. RF geolocation and weather-data niches are competitive and growing, with no unique chokehold position. Microcap scale with persistent operating losses.
